He played professionally for 12 years, including two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Forbes played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]], and the [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass Minutemen]]. ==High school career== Forbes and his mother moved to [[Brooklyn, New York]] when he was a child.{{cite news| url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/colleges/mens_basketball/articles/2007/12/22/umasss_forbes_a_reluctant_leader/ | work=The Boston Globe | first=Marty | last=Dobrow | title=UMass's Forbes a reluctant leader | date=December 22, 2007}} He went on to attend and play basketball at [[Benjamin Banneker Academy]] in Brooklyn. He scored 1,512 points and grabbed 766 rebounds during his high school career, and established career records for points, rebounds, and blocked shots. In local awards, he was selected the [[Newsday]] Player of the Year in Brooklyn as a senior, nominated for City Player of the Year, and earned first-team All-City and All-Tri-State honors. He was also a [[McDonald's]] All-American finalist.{{cite web|url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/forbes_gary00.html|title=Gary Forbes Bio – University of Massachusetts Official Athletic Site|publisher=Umassathletics.com|access-date=October 15, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231151108/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/forbes_gary00.html|archive-date=December 31, 2014}} As a junior, Forbes averaged 27 points, 11 rebounds and six assists a game. As a senior, he averaged 31 points, 13 rebounds, three assists, and three blocked shots a game. That year, he scored 30 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in Benjamin Banneker's 75–69 loss to Lincoln High School in the [[PSAL|Public School Athletic League]] "A" Championship game at [[Madison Square Garden]]. ==College career== Forbes was ranked as the #4 shooting guard, and the #20 overall prospect on ESPN's Top 100 for the incoming class of 2003.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/s/030703topshootingguards.html |title=ESPN.com: RECRUITING – Top Shooting guards |publisher=ESPN |date=2003-05-20 |access-date=October 15, 2013}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/s/020703top100.html |title=ESPN.com: RECRUITING – Recruiting: Top 100 |publisher=ESPN |date=2003-05-15 |access-date=October 15, 2013}} He committed to play at the [[University of Virginia]], after also receiving scholarship offers from [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]] and [[Mississippi State University|Mississippi State]].{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/louisville/basketball/recruiting/player-Gary-Forbes-4667 |title=Gary Forbes – Yahoo! Sports |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |date=April 20, 2011|access-date=October 15, 2013}} Coach [[Pete Gillen]]'s group of newcomers was ranked #17 on the list of top recruiting classes on [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web |url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=910&CID=188535 |title=Rivals.com Basketball Recruiting – Class of 2003 – Top Recruiting Classes |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=May 17, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200517172050/https://n.rivals.com/ |url-status=dead }} As a freshman in 2003–04, Forbes played in all of Virginia's 31 games, starting in 17. He averaged 7.6 points and 4.0 rebounds per game. He finished second on the team in blocked shots (28) and steals (30). Tallied 22 points (season-high) and 9 rebounds against [[University of Minnesota|Minnesota]] in the [[ACC – Big Ten Challenge]].{{cite web |url=http://virginiasports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/120303aaa.html |title=Cavaliers Improve To 4–0 With ACC-Big Ten Challenge Victory – VIRGINIASPORTS.COM – The University of Virginia Official Athletic Site |publisher=Virginiasports.cstv.com |date=December 3, 2003 |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=March 6, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306114035/http://virginiasports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/120303aaa.html |url-status=dead }} As a sophomore in 2004–05, Forbes played in 29 games, started 4, and averaged 9.4 points and 4.1 rebounds per game. Scored 23 (season-high), on 8–11 shooting, in a loss at #4 [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|North Carolina]].{{cite web |url=http://virginiasports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021605aaa.html |title=Virginia Falls To No. 4 North Carolina, 85–61 – VIRGINIASPORTS.COM – The University of Virginia Official Athletic Site |publisher=Virginiasports.cstv.com |date=February 16, 2005 |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=March 6, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306114047/http://virginiasports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021605aaa.html |url-status=dead }} After starting the game at [[Duke University|Duke]], Forbes tallied a double-double with 17 points and 10 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.fansonly.com/schools/va/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/011605aaa.html |title=Virginia Falls To No. 5 Duke, 80–66 – VIRGINIASPORTS.COM – The University of Virginia Official Athletic Site |publisher=Fansonly.com |date=January 16, 2005|access-date=October 15, 2013}} Gillen resigned from Virginia after the end of the 2004–05 season, and Forbes decided to transfer out of the school. He transferred to the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst|University of Massachusetts]], and due to [[NCAA]] transfer rules, he was forced to sit out the 2005–06 season. In the 2006–07 season, his first with the [[UMass Minutemen basketball|Minutemen]], Forbes started in 23 of the team's 33 games. Playing behind established seniors [[Rashaun Freeman]] and [[Stéphane Lasme]], Forbes still averaged 13.0 points and 5.8 rebounds per game. He scored a career-high 31 points and grabbed 14 rebounds in a game at [[Temple University|Temple]].{{cite web |url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021107aaa.html |title=Forbes Goes For 31, But Minutemen Fall To Temple, 98–89 – University of Massachusetts Official Athletic Site |publisher=Umassathletics.com |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=April 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414221002/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021107aaa.html |url-status=dead }} Forbes scored 20 or more points on three other occasions and snared 16 rebounds in a game versus [[University of Richmond|Richmond]].{{cite web |url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/020307aaa.html |title=Forbes & Lowe Push UMass Past Richmond, 72–56 – University of Massachusetts Official Athletic Site |publisher=Umassathletics.com |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=April 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414213814/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/020307aaa.html |url-status=dead }} Helped the Minutemen win their first [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] title since the 1995–96 season. UMass also advanced to the second round of the [[2007 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], their first post-season play since the 1999–2000 season. Coming into his senior year in 2007–08, Forbes was named to the Preseason Atlantic 10 Third Team.{{cite web |url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102507aaa.html |title=Gary Forbes Named Preseason Third Team All-Conference – University of Massachusetts Official Athletic Site |publisher=Umassathletics.com |date=October 25, 2007 |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=April 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414205858/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102507aaa.html |url-status=dead }} By the end of the regular season, he was averaging 20.3 points per game, tied for the league lead in scoring with Temple's [[Dionte Christmas]].{{cite web |url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031008aaa.html |title=Forbes Claims A-10 Player Of Year; Harris Named A-10 Most Improved Player – University of Massachusetts Official Athletic Site |publisher=Umassathletics.com |date=March 10, 2008 |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=April 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414213934/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031008aaa.html |url-status=dead }} Forbes scored 25 or more points on six occasions, including a 29-point high at [[University of Northern Iowa|Northern Iowa]]. The A-10 honored him as the league's [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]] and also placed him on the all-conference First Team. Forbes helped UMass make a deep run in the [[2008 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], advancing past [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]], two-time defending NCAA champion [[University of Florida|Florida]], and on to the final before falling to [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]]. He was named to the NIT's All-Tournament team. Forbes scored a total of 1,639 points over his college career (698 at Virginia, 1,128 at UMass). ==Professional career== After UMass, Forbes participated in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] Pre-Draft Camp in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]] in the summer of 2008.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_prospects_081104.html |title=NBA Development League: 2008 NBA D-League Draft: Top Prospects |work=NBA.com |date=November 5, 2008|access-date=October 15, 2013}} However, he was not selected in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. The [[Washington Wizards]] invited him to participate in their summer mini-camp, and he played in all 5 games, but he only averaged 3.8 points and 0.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizsummercamp_080707.html |title=The Official Site Of The Washington Wizards |work=NBA.com|access-date=October 15, 2013}} In August 2008, Forbes had signed with Italian club [[S.S. Basket Napoli|Basket Napoli]], but the team soon dissolved.{{cite web|url=https://thehoop.blogspot.com/2008/09/forbes-and-dickens-are-leaving-napoli.html |title=The Hoop: Forbes and Dickens are leaving Napoli |publisher=Thehoop.blogspot.com |date=September 24, 2008|access-date=October 15, 2013}} Forbes was selected as the #4 overall pick in the [[2008 NBA Development League draft]], by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web |url=http://umassathletics.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/110708aaa.html Played in 15 games, averaged 13.3 ppg.{{cite web|url=http://www.usbasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=USA&PlayerID=36144 |title=Gary Forbes Player Profile, Brooklyn N., International Stats, Game Logs |publisher=Usbasket |access-date=October 15, 2013}} * 2010: played for [[Ironi Ramat Gan|Ironi Kfar Hamaccabia Ramat Gan]] in the [[Israeli Basketball Super League]]. The club started 2–11 before Forbes joined, then went 4–5 the rest of the regular season with him. Forbes scored 28 in his team debut,{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2010/0221_437_1824.asp |title=European Basketball Main Page |publisher=Eurobasket |date=February 21, 2010|access-date=October 15, 2013}} then went on to average 20.3 ppg (best in the league).{{cite web |url=http://www.hoopsworld.com/Story.asp?story_id=17717 |title=Nothing found for Story Asp?story_id=17717 |publisher=Hoopsworld.com |date=June 16, 2013 |access-date=October 15, 2013 |archive-date=March 14, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314054312/http://www.hoopsworld.com/Story.asp?story_id=17717 |url-status=dead }} However, the team's poor season record forced them to the Relegation Playoffs, where they lost their series, and would be demoted to the [[Liga Leumit (basketball)|National League]] in the 2010–11 season. In July 2010, Forbes returned to the US for another shot at the NBA. He was invited to play with the [[Houston Rockets]] on their summer league team in [[Las Vegas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/summer_league_rosters_2010.html |title=NBA Development League: Former NBA D-League Players In Las Vegas Summer League |work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2010|access-date=October 15, 2013}} Forbes played in 4 of the team's 5 games, averaging 3.8 points and 3.0 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2010/players/gary_forbes/index.html |title=2010 NBA Summer League |work=NBA.com|access-date=October 15, 2013}} On September 18, 2010, the [[Denver Nuggets]] invited Forbes to a training camp.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/9/18/1695952/denver-nuggets-invite-shane|title=Denver Nuggets Invite Shane Edwards, Courtney Sims And Gary Forbes To Training Camp|first=Scott|last=Schroeder|date=18 September 2010|website=Ridiculousupside.com|access-date=23 November 2021}} Playing in 8 games, Forbes averaged 19.0 minutes, 10.1 points, and 2.9 rebounds per game. He replaced [[Al Thornton]] on the team.{{cite web|last=Pastuszek|first=Jon|title=Forbes for Thornton in Guangsha one of several mid-season import moves|url=http://www.niubball.com/2012/12/forbes-for-thornton-in-guangsha-one-of-several-mid-season-import-moves/|publisher=NiuBBall.com|access-date=December 14, 2012|date=December 14, 2012}} In September 2013, Forbes signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/09/28/brooklyn-nets-announce-training-camp-roster|title=Brooklyn Nets Announce Training Camp Roster|website=Nba.com|access-date=23 November 2021}} However, he was waived on October 17.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-gary-forbes|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Gary Forbes|website=Nba.com|access-date=23 November 2021}} On November 1, 2013, Forbes was acquired by the [[Springfield Armor]].{{cite web|title=Returning Players Highlight Initial Training Camp Invites |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/returning_players_for_2013201_2013_11_01.html |work=NBA.com |date=November 1, 2013 |access-date=November 1, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204005917/http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/returning_players_for_2013201_2013_11_01.html |archive-date=December 4, 2013}} On January 3, 2014, he was waived by the Armor due to a season-ending injury. Standings|website=Asia-basket.com|access-date=23 November 2021}} ==National team career== In the summer of 2007, Forbes played with the [[Panama men's national basketball team]] at the [[2007 FIBA Americas Championship]], in [[Las Vegas]]. In four games with the team, he averaged 17.8 points and 4.5 rebounds per game. He scored a game high 29 points against [[Argentine national basketball team|Argentina]]. He was also played with Panama at the [[2011 FIBA Americas Championship]], and the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]].{{Cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Gary%20Forbes/pid//_//players.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605062625/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp/q/Gary%20Forbes/pid/_/players.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 5, 2011|website=Archive.fiba.com|title=Players|access-date=23 November 2021}} ==The Basketball Tournament (TBT)== In the summer of 2017, Forbes competed in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for the Talladega Knights. Competing for the $2 million grand prize, Forbes scored 14 points and grabbed eight rebounds in the Knights' 78–74 first round loss to Paul's Champion's; a team led by former [[NBA]] point guard [[Earl Boykins]]. Forbes also played for Talladega during the summer of 2016. In two games, he averaged 16.0 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists as the Knights fell to the City of Gods in the second round. In TBT 2018, Forbes suited up for Gael Nation. In 2 games, he averaged 6.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 1 assist per game.
